findings.description: The user_data script exports AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY as plaintext static credentials. EC2 user data is readable by anyone with instance metadata access (including via SSRF from the publicly exposed web app) and is stored unencrypted in the instance metadata and Terraform state.
No root_block_device or ebs_block_device encryption is configured, so the instance's boot volume may be created unencrypted, leaving data at rest unprotected.

No metadata_options block is set, so IMDSv1 (token-optional) remains enabled. Combined with the plaintext credentials and public exposure of the host, this makes SSRF-based credential theft from instance metadata straightforward.

The instance is launched in a subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch enabled and routed to an internet gateway, giving it a public IP directly reachable from the internet alongside a security group that allows world-wide SSH.
Ingress on TCP port 22 is open to 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH administrative access to the entire internet and enabling brute-force and exploitation attempts against the publicly addressed web host.

findings.issue_category: unrestricted egress and cleartext HTTP ingress
findings.description: Egress allows all protocols to 0.0.0.0/0, permitting unrestricted data exfiltration and C2 traffic, and ingress permits cleartext HTTP on port 80 from the internet with no TLS-protected alternative.
The EBS volume attached to the web host is created without encryption (encrypted is explicitly commented out), leaving stored data unprotected at rest and readable from raw snapshots or storage.
The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted EBS volume and is therefore itself unencrypted; snapshots are easily shared or copied, spreading unprotected data.
The VPC flow log destination bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so sensitive network telemetry is stored unencrypted.

findings.issue_category: missing public access block and access controls
findings.description: No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, bucket policy enforcing TLS, or versioning is configured for the flow log bucket, so it is not protected against accidental public exposure or cleartext access.
map_public_ip_on_launch is true, so every instance launched in this subnet is automatically given a public IP and directly exposed to the internet with no private-subnet segmentation.
map_public_ip_on_launch is true, automatically exposing all instances launched in this subnet to the internet rather than keeping workloads in private subnets behind NAT.
